issue.title: [vue] When using same query multiple times, one briefly has outdated data on query key changes

repository.name: query
repository.description: 🤖 Powerful asynchronous state management, server-state utilities and data fetching for the web. TS/JS, React Query, Solid Query, Svelte Query and Vue Query.

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

I'm running into some very strange behavior which to me seems like a bug, though I could of course be missing something about Vue's reactivity system or something. Basically when I have two instances of exactly the same query and change the query key, there's a brief period of time after the query key change where one query has its data set to `undefined` while the other query has its data still set to the data for the previous query key.

### Your minimal, reproducible example

https://codesandbox.io/s/agitated-spence-xjd86m?file=/src/App.vue

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the sandbox
2. Look at the console output

### Expected behavior

When I change the query key, I expect the data for both queries to be set to `undefined`. But as you can see from the output, after changing the query key, query 2 still has the old data, while query 1 has `undefined`. After that query 2's data changes to `undefined`, though. Then finally when the promise resolves they both get set to the new data.

Interestingly if you remove one of the queries, it behaves completely as expected, being `undefined` right after the changing and then getting the new data.

### How often does this bug happen?

Every time

body:
I assume this sort here is not stable since a change in 3.2.38 (https://github.com/vuejs/core/commit/78c199d6dbe8931520b75d8bfe0d49366a06922a):

https://github.com/vuejs/core/blob/957722c4185ea87aabc711f6f8997e528dd3ba1b/packages/runtime-core/src/scheduler.ts#L219

The root cause is: the `findInsertionIndex` function returns the same index when job.id is equal, resulting in a misordering of the jobs in the queue.

https://github.com/vuejs/core/blob/957722c4185ea87aabc711f6f8997e528dd3ba1b/packages/runtime-core/src/apiWatch.ts#L362
this resulted in the same jobId

issue.title: fix(runtime-core): ensure jobs are in the correct order

issue.body:
Fixes #7576.

There is an existing PR to fix this issue, #7622, but I believe it introduces some new problems. The changes to `findInsertionIndex()` that I'm proposing here are quite different to the changes in that PR, so I decided it was better to open a new PR rather than just adding review feedback to the existing PR.

The additions to the first test case are exactly the same as in #7622, confirming that this fix also fixes the original problem. I've then added an extra test case, checking some of the edge cases that #7622 misses.

Whether the new job is `pre: true` doesn't affect the insertion point. Either way, the job should be inserted after any `pre` jobs with the same id. If there is a job with the same id without `pre: true` (there can only be one in the active part of the queue) then the insertion point should be before that job.
